_note: The coaches by the track (GDD 4.3.1, step R4; user 2026-10-09: 'coach personality is key, every coach cannot be the same'). Every coach is a personality with his own words. The club coach of a career is one of `pool`, picked from a hash of the athlete's name (Coaches.id_of), so the same career always has the same coach; a hired coach (the Coaching step, later) sets Athlete.coach_id. All names are made up. A coach speaks only about what he can see from his spot (outdoors in the stands by the 200 m start, indoors in the stands at the rail of the hall; races.json controls.coach). Placeholders: {name} a rival's surname, {split} the player's time at the mark, {pos} the player's place (3rd), {gap} metres to the leader, {to_go} metres to go, {m} metres. talk = how often he speaks unprompted (1 = the base chances in race_commentary.json coach), gap_s = race seconds between his lines at least. shouts = the words on the decision cards (card id -> answer id -> text); the default wording is race_cards.json coach.shouts. lines = what he calls during the race: split_* when the player passes his spot (front = leading, back = 12 m or more behind the leader, hard = the Feeling word says hurting or empty, ok = the rest), rival_kick / rival_move (a rival goes near the player), player_kick, boxed, fall, dropped, lead (the player takes the lead), good / bad (a verdict on a choice 10 s later), finish_win / finish_podium / finish_other (when the player crosses the line). finish_part = the finish of a heat or section place that is no medal (decision 43). story = his one line in the Race story, by case (RaceStory picks the first that fits: dnf, dq, fell, won, won_part (won a heat / section), kick_died, boxed, too_fast, faded, good_kick, podium, better, as_expected, below).

calm.name: Marja Hakala
calm.title: The calm technician
calm.blurb: Quiet and exact. Few words, mostly about rhythm and relaxing. Never raises her voice.

break.lead: Go on, smoothly to the front.

fall.chase: Up. Rhythm first, then catch them.

box.ease: Drop back a step and go round.

slow.lead: Take it up. Easy and even.

rival_kick: Let {name} go. Think of your own kick.
fall: Up, up. Slowly back into it.
lead: Easy. You don't have to run away.
bad: Don't worry about it. Next step.
finish_win: Yes. You did it so calmly.
finish_podium: Good race. We'll talk about it later.
Well done. Breathe, walk it out.
finish_other: Walk it out. We'll look at it together.
It's done. Breathe. We learn from it.
finish_part: Good. Walk it out. We'll see what the times say.
Done. Breathe. Rest the legs now.

dnf: Rest first. We'll look at what happened another day.
You were hurt. Nothing more to say today.
dq: A rule is a rule. We'll practise running a cleaner line.
fell: A fall is not your fault. You got up and finished, and that matters.
The fall cost the race, not your running. Rest well.
won: A very controlled race. That is exactly how we practised it.
You stayed relaxed and it showed. Well run.
won_part: You won it calmly, and that is all it needed to be. Now rest.
A controlled win. Keep the legs fresh for what comes next.
kick_died: You went a little too early. Your kick is good, we just need to wait for it.
The kick started too far out. Trust the last 200.
boxed: You lost time in the traffic. Next time look for the space earlier.
Boxed in too long. We'll work on moving out in time.
too_fast: The first lap was a bit hard. Keep the first 400 calmer.
You went out too fast and paid for it. Rhythm first.
faded: You faded at the end. We'll build the finish in training.
The last 200 was heavy. That is trainable.
good_kick: A very good finish. Patience first, then strength.
You waited well and used the finish.
podium: A good race. A place on the podium is earned.
Good running. You were with them to the end.
better: Better than the numbers said. That's a good sign.
You beat what we expected. Let's keep this feeling.
as_expected: Right where we expected. A solid race.
A steady, honest race. Build on it.
below: Not your best. Don't worry, we'll see what it taught us.
Below what you can do. Sleep, eat, and we look at it.

drill.name: Pekka Rautio
drill.title: The hard driver
drill.blurb: Loud and demanding. Pushes hard, praises rarely, and says it straight when a choice was poor.

break.shoulder: Stay on their shoulder. Don't drop back!
break.back: Stay back, but keep your head up!

bell.push: Push! Now! This is the lap!
bell.hold: Hold it! Don't let anything go!
bell.ease: Back off a bit. Save it!

fall.steady: Get up and finish it! No stopping!

kick.wait: Hold! Wait for the straight! Hold!

dropped.dig: Dig! DIG! Hang on to them!
dropped.own: Your own pace! Don't blow up!

split_hard: {split}! Too hot! Cool down a bit!
fall: Get up! The race isn't over!
finish_win: Yes!! That's what I'm talking about!
finish_podium: Fine. Next time, the top step.
finish_other: That wasn't enough. We talk in the morning.
Not good enough. You know it.
finish_part: Done. Now wait for the times. Don't sit around.

dnf: That was not a race. We rest, then we find out why.
A DNF. Rest. Then we work.
fell: You fell and you got up. That's the only good thing I can say.
The fall decided it. Next time you're not the one on the ground.
won: That was a win. I won't say more, don't get cocky.
Won. Good. Now we want to run it faster.
won_part: You won it. It's a heat, not a title. Don't get cocky.
Won the round. Good. Now save something for the next one.
kick_died: You kicked from too far. Do that again and I'll stand there with a stopwatch until you learn.
You went too early and died. Be patient!
boxed: You sat in the box like a tourist. Get out of there next time!
Boxed in and passive. That is a decision, and it was a poor one.
too_fast: You went out like a rocket and paid for it. First lap, think!
Too hot, too early. You gave that race away on lap one.
faded: The last 200 was weak. We'll fix that in training. Hard.
You died at the end. More work. Much more.
good_kick: Good finish. That is the kind of kick I want.
You hit them at the end. Good. Now do it from further out.
podium: A podium. Good. But I've seen you do more.
On the podium, fine. We want better.
better: Better than anyone expected. Don't let it go to your head.
You beat the odds. Now do it again.
as_expected: As expected. That is not enough if you want more.
A race of the right level. Next one needs more.
below: That was below you. I expect more.
Not good. You know it. Work harder.

warm.name: Anneli Saarinen
warm.title: The warm mentor
warm.blurb: Encouraging and caring. Always on your side, quick to praise, gentle when things go wrong.

break.lead: Go for it! You can lead!

fall.chase: You can still get them! Go!

box.push: Go for the gap, you can do it!

move.wait: Let {name} go, you'll get them back!

dropped.own: It's fine, run your own pace!

slow.lead: Go on, take it, you're ready!

rival_kick: {name} is going, but you've got this!
Don't worry about {name}, wait for yours!
rival_move: {name} is moving! You decide, you're doing great!
fall: Oh no! Up you get, you're fine!
Get up! Finish it, you can!
bad: It's all right, just keep going!
No worries, you'll get it back!
finish_win: You did it! I'm so proud of you!
YES! You won! Oh, well done!
finish_other: It's all right, you tried so hard!
Come here. You did well. We'll go through it together.
finish_part: Well run! Now let's see what the times say.
That's done, you ran so well. Rest your legs.

dnf: Rest and be kind to yourself. There will be other races.
You couldn't go on, and that's all right. We'll come back stronger.
dq: That was a shame, but it's a lesson. We'll run it clean next time.
fell: You fell and still got up and finished. I am very proud of that.
The fall wasn't your fault. Go and get a good rest.
won: You won! I'm so proud of you. You ran it beautifully.
A win, and a lovely race. Enjoy it!
won_part: You won it! A lovely run. Now rest well.
A win in your round, and so smoothly! Well done.
kick_died: You were brave to go early, even if it cost the finish. We'll work on the timing.
The kick started a bit early, but it was a brave one.
boxed: The traffic wasn't kind to you. We'll practise finding the space.
You got stuck, and that happens. Next time you'll find the gap sooner.
too_fast: You were so eager at the start! We'll practise the first lap together.
You went out fast because you're strong. Next time, a bit calmer.
faded: The end was tough, but you kept fighting. That's what I saw.
You were tired at the end, that's normal. We'll build that.
good_kick: Your finish was lovely! You waited and then went for it.
That finish was so strong. You should be proud.
podium: On the podium! I am so happy for you.
A medal! You earned every metre of it.
better: Better than anyone expected! Well done!
You beat the expectations. I knew you could.
as_expected: A good, solid race. Right where we hoped.
A nice honest race. We'll build from here.
below: It wasn't your day, and that's all right. Rest, we'll go again.
Not your best, but you gave your all. That's what counts.

tactician.name: Heikki Laine
tactician.title: The race reader
tactician.blurb: Reads the race like a chess game. Short, factual, names rivals and gaps, and explains the why.

break.lead: Take it. Nobody else wants it.
break.shoulder: Third or fourth. Stay close, stay covered.
break.back: Back of the pack, out of trouble.

bell.push: You have the legs. Press on now.
bell.hold: Hold your place. The race starts at 200.
bell.ease: Too fast for you. Back off, save it.

fall.chase: Get on them. They'll be slow in the last 200.
fall.steady: Finish steady, no point in blowing up.

kick.now: Go now. You can hold it.
kick.wait: Wait. Hold it until the straight.

box.wait: Wait. The gap comes in a second.
box.ease: Drop back a stride and go round.
box.push: The gap is there. Take it now.

move.go: Go with {name}. That pace won't last.

straight.wide: Go wide. Don't wait for the inside.
straight.inside: Stay in. It opens in a moment.

dropped.dig: Close it. It's still only a few metres.
dropped.own: Let them go. You'll pass them later.

slow.lead: Take the lead. They're all waiting.
slow.stay: Stay where you are. They are slow, let them.

split_front: {split}. Good, but they're on your heels.
split_back: {split}. Too far back. Get closer before the bell.
split_hard: {split}. Too fast for you. Back off.
rival_kick: {name} is kicking. Early. That won't last.
{name} goes from far out. Don't go yet.
rival_move: {name} goes. Ask yourself if you can match that.
boxed: Ease and go round, or wait. Decide.
fall: Get up. There's still time to pick people off.
dropped: Keep them in sight. They'll come back.
lead: You lead. Control it, don't speed up.
good: Good decision. Look at the gap.
finish_win: Perfectly read. That was your race from the start.
Won it exactly where it was there to win.
finish_podium: Podium. One decision away from the top.
Good. Look at the video, there's something to take.
finish_other: We'll go through it tonight. There were chances.
The race had other options. We'll look.
finish_part: Done. Now the times from the other races decide. Recover.
Place noted. The overall result comes after the others.

dnf: No result. We analyse after you've rested.
A DNF. Nothing to read from a race that stops.
dq: Obstruction. The line choice at the finish was wrong. We'll go through it.
fell: The fall decided the race. Nothing to learn but that bunched fields are risky.
A fall. You lost the race there, not on the track.
won: You read it right and went at the right moment. A textbook win.
The win came from the timing. Keep it.
won_part: You won the round by reading it right. The overall picture comes from the times.
A round win from the timing. Now see what the others run.
kick_died: The kick began too far out. Your kick is worth about 150, not 300.
You kicked early and paid for it in the last 100. Timing.
boxed: The box cost you the race. Look for the outside earlier.
Boxed at the wrong time. Position before the bell, not after.
too_fast: First lap faster than your fitness. The last 200 paid for it.
You spent the energy before the race started. Lap one is the problem.
faded: You lost places in the last 200. The pace was right, the energy wasn't.
A fade at the end. The tempo was fine, the strength wasn't.
good_kick: Well timed. You kicked when the others had nothing left.
The finish won you places. The positioning set it up.
podium: A podium by choices and legs both. One tactical step to the top.
You earned the podium. Next time, the second lap faster.
better: You finished above your ranking on paper. Racing smarter than your numbers.
as_expected: Finished where the numbers say. No big mistakes, no big gains.
A fair result. The race gave nothing extra.
below: Below your ranking on paper. We'll find the mistake.
Worse than the numbers predict. The race wasn't read right.
